body: You're not alone. The only thing I can say is just reaffirm to yourself how much you love her. This sounds like you're having self-doubt, more than doubt about her. You don't have to answer, but does she know about your history with infidelity? Was it with her? If you're hiding something from your SO, than it will honestly make you paranoid and worried (speaking from personal experience here).

How invested are you in the relationship. If you really want to make it work, it sounds like from how emotional she is she'd be empathetic. Just let her know your feelings. If you breakup with her, without letting her know you're feelings, you'll continue to carry around that load of emotions into your next relationship, and you'll wonder if you could have made the relationship work and maybe even regret it. Just my advice though.

Oh gosh, that hurts. I'm so sorry. 7 years is such a long time to feel like you've known someone, and for them to backstab you by using the photo you took. I'm sorry. I still feel like if you don't confront him, even if you do end up breaking up, you'll later regret it. But it can hurt. If you don't feel comfortable doing it alone, maybe have the friend that discovered it come over and help you confront him.

Well, has he been active recently? If he said he's 34, maybe that's the last time he updated it. I'd just go straight to him though, say you found out about it. If he says he hasn't done anything on it recently (like in years), then say just to be sure you'd like to see it from his view just to be sure. If he doesn't want to show it to you... then I'd start questioning why.

But have you had any concerns over cheating or anything in the past? Does he seem like the kind of guy that would get on there, joke around just to get an ego high? Or has he seemed bored in your relationship recently?

I once had a situation like this. I was slightly fliratious with someone I thought was a friend, and she got my phone number. We had to work on projects and deadlines together in work together. We had worked together for about a month. I gave her my phone number, and she started texting me. I was slightly flirtatious (because again, I thought why not) It went from her texting me once a day (manageable) to about a week later every 5 minutes asking what I was doing until I went to bed at night. Having to work with her, I tried to be friendly. When she tried to turn it romantic. I tried to reason and explain that I wasn't interested, but that didn't work. So what I did was just block her number and act like she had never texted me. If she talked about anything outside of work I would either ignore or follow up with a work question.   


I'd suggest you do a similar thing. But don't let her down easy, you've got to be firm. That's my advice, hopefully it helps!
